findings.text: The first sentence tells a newcomer what Athena is, and the next two paragraphs say what a study is and why this one exists. That covers 'what is it' within a few seconds of reading.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: A next step is offered at the top and links to a dedicated section, so the reader never has to hunt for what to do.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The install step assumes the reader already has a checkout and knows what setup.sh needs. The page gives no clone command, no prerequisites (a Rust toolchain? model API keys?) and doesn't say which repository to run `athena ask "add a changelog"` in.
findings.source: Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh

findings.text: These are the reasons a newcomer would care about Athena, but nothing on the page shows them: no example request, no checker verdict, no cost record. The page only shows Athena's study output. 'Why it matters' therefore rests on two sentences.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The firstmate study is well built for a first-time reader. It has a one-line definition, a 'Words used first' list placed before the terms are used, a numbered walk through one task, and a separate list of failures and missing limits.

Several terms the reader needs are never defined. 'Captain call' (used in t9 and ra5) has no glossary entry, the 'stale wake' entry never says what a wake is, and 'endpoint', 'durable record' and 'harness pin' appear without explanation.
findings.source: open captain call; stale wake: A wake after which the agent inspects a worker…

findings.text: The Counters section says t9 (ready → reopened) changes places-held, but the t9 card says nothing about places. A careful reader can't check this link.
findings.source: places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11

findings.text: Every statement links to a claim, and every claim links to exact file lines at a pinned commit. This backs up the page's main promise and gives a skeptical reader a concrete way to check it.
findings.source: Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end.

findings.text: 'About this page' points to a studies/ folder without saying which repository it is in or linking to it, so a newcomer can't follow the pointer.
findings.source: This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from.
